Therapy that takes the slow road. By design.

I'm Maren Ahoyade. I've been a Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist in Oregon since 2014. My practice is small on purpose — twenty-two clients on the calendar, no more — and the work I do is mostly with adults processing trauma and couples in long-term relationships. We meet weekly for fifty minutes. We do not rush.

About me, with the credentials in plain order.

I earned my MA in Marriage and Family Therapy from Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education in 2013, and I've been licensed in Oregon (LMFT #T1538) since November 2014. Before private practice I spent four years on staff at Trillium Family Services in northeast Portland, primarily with adolescents and young adults processing complex trauma.

I am EMDR-trained (Level 2, EMDRIA-approved, 2017), Internal Family Systems–informed (Level 1, 2019, with ongoing consultation under Dr. Annette Holcomb), and I incorporate cognitive-behavioral structure when the work calls for it. I am not a one-modality practitioner. I do not believe trauma yields to a single tool. The session shape we develop is yours, not mine.

I am a queer, mixed-race therapist (Yoruba and Norwegian heritage) and my practice is welcoming to LGBTQ+, BIPOC, and trauma-survivor clients in particular — though anyone who feels we might be a good fit is welcome to reach out. I do not work with active addiction, eating disorders that require medical monitoring, or active suicidal crisis — I will refer you with care to colleagues who specialize there.

props.title: EMDR for trauma
props.description: Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing. Effective when there is a discrete event or series of events the body is still holding. We do not do EMDR until we have built a foundation — usually six to eight sessions of preparation work first.

props.title: Internal Family Systems
props.description: IFS treats the psyche as a system of parts — protective parts, exiled parts, and a core Self. Useful when you find yourself reacting in ways you don't endorse and can't explain. Meaningful for trauma, perfectionism, and inner-critic patterns.

props.title: Couples · Gottman-informed
props.description: For couples I draw heavily on the Gottman Method (Level 1, 2018) — research-backed, structured, and oriented around the actual mechanics of how partners hurt each other and find their way back. We do not coach communication skills; we untangle patterns.

props.question: Do you take insurance?
props.answer: I am out-of-network with all major insurers. I provide a monthly superbill you can submit for partial reimbursement. Most of my clients are reimbursed 30-60% of session cost. I do not handle insurance billing directly so I can keep the practice small.

props.question: How long do clients usually work with you?
props.answer: It varies. The shortest meaningful work I've done is six months (a discrete EMDR-focused trauma piece). The average is around 18 months. The longest is six years (couples work, on and off through life transitions).

props.question: Are you accepting new clients?
props.answer: Sometimes. I keep a maximum of 22 weekly clients. As of January 2026 I have a waitlist of about three months for individual work and one month for couples. The free 20-minute consultation is available immediately.

props.question: What if you're not the right fit?
props.answer: I refer roughly half of consultation calls to colleagues. I keep a referral list of trusted Portland-area therapists with open availability across modalities, identities, and price points. I will help you land somewhere good, even if that's not with me.

props.question: What is your cancellation policy?
props.answer: 24 hours notice for full credit. Late cancellations and no-shows are charged the full session fee — you may use the time for a phone or video session in the same week if you prefer. Three or more late cancellations in a quarter and we'll talk about whether the timing is right.
